newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwean bank cuts base lending rate to 28.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwean bank cuts base lending rate to 28.5 pct.

text.p: Standard Chartered Bank Zimbabwe, one of the country's biggest commercial banks, on Monday lowered its minimum lending rate to 28.5 percent from 30 percent.
"Standard Chartered Bank Zimbabwe will reduce its minimum lending rate by 1.5 percent from 30 percent to 28.5 percent with effect from Monday, October 14," the bank said in a statement.

This is the second time in three months that the bank has lowered its minimum lending rate. In early August, it and other commercial banks eased their rates to 30 percent from 32.5 percent on the back of falling annual inflation and lower money market rates.

Zimbabwean industrialists and capital market analysts have been expecting the banks to lower their lending rates further after the central Reserve Bank in August cut its rediscount rate to 27.50 percent from 29.50.
The Reserve Bank said the lower rediscount rate was due to falling annual inflation which dropped to a three-year low of 17.7 percent in August from 22 percent in July.
